subproblem.title: A constant (n+1)-covector is the exterior derivative of its affine contraction (n+1)⁻¹·ι_{y−x₀}α
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an (n+1)-covector on ℝ^P (α : Covector (Euclid P) (n+1), a continuous alternating (n+1)-linear form) and let x₀ ∈ ℝ^P. Let ψ be the n-form ψ(y) := ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ · α.curryLeft(y − x₀), i.e. ψ(y)(v₁, …, v_n) = (n + 1)⁻¹ · α(y − x₀, v₁, …, v_n). Then for every x ∈ ℝ^P the exterior derivative of ψ at x equals α: extDeriv ψ x = α. Here extDeriv ψ x = alternatizeUncurryFin(fderiv ℝ ψ x) is Mathlib's exterior derivative, which is SimonGMT's exteriorDerivative.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1)) (x₀ x : Euclid P), extDeriv (fun y : Euclid P => ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft (y - x₀)) x = α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof, first half: the homotopy formula for a constant form. With ψ(x) = (n+1)⁻¹·α.curryLeft(x − x₀), dψ(x) = α for every x.

Notation. α.curryLeft : ℝ^P →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n is Mathlib's ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft, with α.curryLeft(v)(v₁, …, v_n) = α(v, v₁, …, v_n) (curryLeft_apply_apply). For an n-form ω, extDeriv ω x := alternatizeUncurryFin(fderiv ℝ ω x) (definition of Mathlib's extDeriv). Put s := ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹, L := α.curryLeft and ψ(y) := s · L(y − x₀).

1. (Derivative of the contraction.) L is a continuous linear map, so it has derivative L at every point, in particular at x − x₀ (ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt). The map y ↦ y − x₀ has the identity as derivative at x (hasFDerivAt_id, HasFDerivAt.sub_const). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp), y ↦ L(y − x₀) has derivative L ∘ id = L at x (ContinuousLinearMap.comp_id).

2. (Constant factor.) Multiplying by the constant s, ψ has derivative s • L at x (HasFDerivAt.const_smul). Hence fderiv ℝ ψ x = s • L (HasFDerivAt.fderiv).

3. (Pull out the scalar.) By definition, extDeriv ψ x = alternatizeUncurryFin(fderiv ℝ ψ x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(s • L) = s • alternatizeUncurryFin(α.curryLeft) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul).

4. (Round trip.) ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft states alternatizeUncurryFin(α.curryLeft) = (n + 1) • α, a natural-number multiple. Indeed alternatizeUncurryFin(f)(v₀, …, v_n) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i f(v_i)(v₀, …, v̂_i, …, v_n). For f = α.curryLeft each summand equals (−1)^i α(v_i, v₀, …, v̂_i, …, v_n) = (−1)^i (−1)^i α(v₀, …, v_n) = α(v₀, …, v_n), because moving v_i to the front costs the sign (−1)^i; so the sum is (n+1)·α(v₀, …, v_n). By Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul, (n + 1) • α = ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) • α = ((n : ℝ) + 1) • α (push_cast).

5. (Conclusion.) Therefore extDeriv ψ x = s • (((n : ℝ) + 1) • α) = (s · ((n : ℝ) + 1)) • α (smul_smul). Since (n : ℝ) + 1 > 0, ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ · ((n : ℝ) + 1) = 1 (inv_mul_cancel₀), so this is 1 • α = α (one_smul). ∎

Lean note (this exact proof compiled against the pinned snapshot in a scratch file; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only):
  intro P n α x₀ x
  have h1 : HasFDerivAt (fun y : Euclid P => α.curryLeft (y - x₀)) α.curryLeft x := by
    have h := (α.curryLeft.hasFDerivAt (x := x - x₀)).comp x ((hasFDerivAt_id x).sub_const x₀)
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_id] at h
    exact h
  have hd : HasFDerivAt (fun y : Euclid P => ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft (y - x₀))
      (((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft) x := h1.const_smul (((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹)
  rw [extDeriv, hd.fderiv, ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul,
    ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft, ← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℝ,
    smul_smul]
  have hn : ((n : ℝ) + 1) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  push_cast
  rw [inv_mul_cancel₀ hn, one_smul]
proof_key_steps: y ↦ α.curryLeft(y − x₀) has derivative α.curryLeft at x (chain rule: a continuous linear map composed with y ↦ y − x₀).
extDeriv ψ x = alternatizeUncurryFin((n+1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft) = (n+1)⁻¹ • alternatizeUncurryFin(α.curryLeft) (alternatizeUncurryFin_smul).
alternatizeUncurryFin(α.curryLeft) = (n+1) • α (alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft with Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul), so extDeriv ψ x = α.

audit.reason: The explicit derivative is the scaled continuous linear map α.curryLeft. The pinned alternatization identity yields (n+1)•α, and the nonzero real scalar n+1 cancels. This proves the exact proposition for every P,n without additional hypotheses or dependencies.

subproblem.title: A current takes the same value on test forms that agree on an open neighbourhood of its support
subproblem.statement: Assume (VO), the exact frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support, which appears verbatim as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U and G be subsets of ℝ^P, let X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k) be a current and let φ₁, φ₂ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (TestFormOn U k) be test forms. Suppose G is open, spt X ⊆ G (X.support, Simon 6.2.11), and φ₁(x) = φ₂(x) for every x ∈ G. Then X(φ₁) = X(φ₂).
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U G : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (φ₁ φ₂ : TestFormOn U k), IsOpen G → X.support ⊆ G → EqOn (φ₁ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) (φ₂ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) G → X φ₁ = X φ₂
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (localization by (VO)), stated for two arbitrary test forms that agree on an open set G ⊇ spt X. In parent step 6 one takes U = ℝ^P, φ₁ = φ, φ₂ = ζφ and G = B_{ϱ+ε/2}(x₀).

1. (The difference is a test form.) TestFormOn U k is a submodule of the k-forms, so φ := φ₁ − φ₂ ∈ TestFormOn U k. Its underlying form is x ↦ φ₁(x) − φ₂(x) (Submodule.coe_sub).

2. (Where φ vanishes.) For x ∈ G, φ(x) = φ₁(x) − φ₂(x) = 0 by hypothesis. Hence support φ = {x : φ(x) ≠ 0} ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ G.

3. (Topological support.) G is open, so ℝ^P ∖ G is closed (IsOpen.isClosed_compl). A closed set containing support φ contains its closure, so tsupport φ = closure(support φ) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ G (closure_minimal).

4. (Disjointness.) spt X = X.support ⊆ G and tsupport φ ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ G, and G and ℝ^P ∖ G are disjoint. Hence tsupport φ and spt X are disjoint (Disjoint.mono applied to disjoint_compl_left).

5. (Apply (VO).) (VO) with (P, k, U, S := X, ω := φ) gives X(φ) = 0.

6. (Linearity.) X acts through the linear map X.toCurrent, so X(φ₁ − φ₂) = X(φ₁) − X(φ₂) (LinearMap.map_sub). By step 5, X(φ₁) − X(φ₂) = 0, i.e. X(φ₁) = X(φ₂). ∎

Lean note (this exact proof compiled against the pinned snapshot in a scratch file; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only):
  intro VO P k U G X φ₁ φ₂ hG hspt heq
  have hsub : tsupport ((φ₁ - φ₂ : TestFormOn U k) : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ⊆ Gᶜ := by
    apply closure_minimal _ hG.isClosed_compl
    intro x hx hxG
    apply hx
    change (φ₁ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x - (φ₂ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x = 0
    rw [heq hxG, sub_self]
  have hdisj : Disjoint (tsupport ((φ₁ - φ₂ : TestFormOn U k) : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k))
      X.support :=
    Disjoint.mono hsub hspt disjoint_compl_left
  have h := VO P k U X (φ₁ - φ₂) hdisj
  have h2 := X.toCurrent.map_sub φ₁ φ₂
  change X (φ₁ - φ₂) = X φ₁ - X φ₂ at h2
  linarith
proof_key_steps: φ₁ − φ₂ is a test form in U that vanishes on G.
Gᶜ is closed, so tsupport(φ₁ − φ₂) ⊆ Gᶜ, which is disjoint from spt X ⊆ G.
(VO) gives X(φ₁ − φ₂) = 0, and linearity gives X(φ₁) = X(φ₂).

audit.reason: The difference is a test form vanishing on G. Openness places its topological support in Gᶜ, disjoint from X.support. The verbatim VO hypothesis and linearity give equality of evaluations. All hypotheses are present, and the proof has no circular reliance.

subproblem.title: Test forms are Lipschitz in the Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (TestFormOn U k: a C^∞ k-form on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U). For a k-covector β write |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β, the Euclidean coefficient norm of Simon 6.1.15. Then there is a real number c ≥ 0 such that |ω(x) − ω(y)| ≤ c·dist(x, y) for all x, y ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U k), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c ∧ ∀ x y : Euclid P, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x - (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y) ≤ c * dist x y
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 4 of the parent proof (the Lipschitz constant c of the fixed test form, measured in the Euclidean coefficient norm), stated for an arbitrary degree k and an arbitrary domain U. The comparison of the coefficient norm with the operator norm (parent step 2) is supplied by part (iii) of the sibling norm_props.

Notation. For a k-covector β (an element of Covector (Euclid P) k, i.e. a continuous alternating k-linear form on ℝ^P), |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β and ‖β‖ is its operator norm. On ℝ^P, ‖·‖ is the Euclidean norm and dist(x, y) = ‖x − y‖ (dist_eq_norm). Write w := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) k for the underlying form of ω.

1. (Coefficient norm versus operator norm.) By the sibling norm_props, part (iii), applied to (P, k), there is a real C ≥ 0 such that |β| ≤ C·‖β‖ for every k-covector β.

2. (Smoothness.) Membership ω ∈ TestFormOn U k means IsTestForm w ∧ tsupport w ⊆ U, where IsTestForm w = IsSmoothForm w ∧ HasCompactSupport w and IsSmoothForm w = ContDiff ℝ ∞ w. Since the smoothness order ∞ is nonzero, w is differentiable at every point of ℝ^P (ContDiff.differentiable). Its Fréchet derivative Dw := fderiv ℝ w : ℝ^P → (ℝ^P →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) k) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv).

3. (The derivative is bounded.) Dw has compact support because w does (HasCompactSupport.fderiv: the support of Dw lies in tsupport w). A continuous map with compact support into a normed space is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), so there is L ∈ ℝ with ‖Dw(z)‖ ≤ L for every z ∈ ℝ^P. Put L₀ := max(L, 0). Then L₀ ≥ 0 and ‖Dw(z)‖ ≤ L₀ for every z.

4. (Mean value inequality.) ℝ^P is convex, w is differentiable at every point, and ‖Dw(z)‖ ≤ L₀ for every z. The mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le with s = ℝ^P) therefore gives ‖w(x) − w(y)‖ ≤ L₀·‖x − y‖ for all x, y ∈ ℝ^P.

5. (Conclusion.) Put c := C·L₀, which is ≥ 0 as a product of nonnegative reals. For all x, y ∈ ℝ^P, step 1 (applied to β := w(x) − w(y)), step 4 and C ≥ 0 give
   |w(x) − w(y)| ≤ C·‖w(x) − w(y)‖ ≤ C·(L₀·‖x − y‖) = c·‖x − y‖ = c·dist(x, y).
This is the claim. ∎

Lean note (this exact proof compiled against the pinned snapshot in a scratch file; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only). Supplying f explicitly in Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support is necessary: without (f := …) elaboration hits a whnf heartbeat timeout.
  intro P k U ω
  obtain ⟨C, hC0, hC⟩ := (Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props P k).2.2.1
  have hsm : IsSmoothForm (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) := ω.property.1.1
  have hcs : HasCompactSupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) := ω.property.1.2
  have hcont : Continuous (fderiv ℝ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) :=
    hsm.continuous_fderiv (by simp)
  have hcs' : HasCompactSupport (fderiv ℝ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) := hcs.fderiv ℝ
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ : ∃ L : ℝ, ∀ z, ‖fderiv ℝ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) z‖ ≤ L :=
    Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support
      (f := fderiv ℝ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) hcont hcs'
  have hdiff : Differentiable ℝ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) :=
    hsm.differentiable (by simp)
  have hmv : ∀ x y : Euclid P, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x -
      (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y‖ ≤ max L 0 * ‖x - y‖ := fun x y =>
    convex_univ.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le (fun z _ => hdiff z)
      (fun z _ => (hL z).trans (le_max_left _ _)) (mem_univ y) (mem_univ x)
  refine ⟨C * max L 0, mul_nonneg hC0 (le_max_right _ _), fun x y => ?_⟩
  have h1 := hC ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x - (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y)
  have h2 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hmv x y) hC0
  rw [dist_eq_norm]
  calc covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x -
        (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y)
      ≤ C * ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x - (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y‖ := h1
    _ ≤ C * (max L 0 * ‖x - y‖) := h2
    _ = C * max L 0 * ‖x - y‖ := by ring
proof_key_steps: norm_props (iii): |β| ≤ C‖β‖ for every k-covector β, with C ≥ 0.
ω is C^∞ with compact support, so Dω is continuous with compact support; hence ‖Dω(z)‖ ≤ L₀ for all z, with L₀ ≥ 0.
Mean value inequality on the convex set ℝ^P: ‖ω(x) − ω(y)‖ ≤ L₀‖x − y‖.
c := C·L₀ ≥ 0 gives |ω(x) − ω(y)| ≤ c·dist(x, y).

audit.reason: Global smoothness and compact support give a continuous, compactly supported derivative and hence a uniform bound. The mean value inequality and norm_props produce the stated nonnegative coefficient-norm Lipschitz constant. No openness assumption on U is needed. The supplied proof compiles using only its declared dependency.

subproblem.title: A cycle supported in an open ball annihilates every test form that is constant on that ball
subproblem.statement: Assume (VO), the exact frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support, which appears verbatim as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let X ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ (n+1)) be a current, x₀ ∈ ℝ^P, r a real number with r > 0, α an (n+1)-covector (Covector (Euclid P) (n+1)) and φ ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ (n+1)) a test form. Suppose ∂X = 0 (X.boundary = 0), spt X ⊆ B_r(x₀) (the open ball), and φ(x) = α for every x ∈ B_r(x₀). Then X(φ) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)) (x₀ : Euclid P) (r : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1)) (φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)), 0 < r → X.boundary = 0 → X.support ⊆ ball x₀ r → (∀ x ∈ ball x₀ r, (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (n + 1)) x = α) → X φ = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 and 7 of the parent proof (cut-off, and 'constant forms are boundaries near spt X'). Here the cut-off is taken at inner radius r, and the parent's test form ζα is replaced by any test form φ that equals α on B_r(x₀). The (VO)-localization of parent step 6 is the sibling localize, and the identity dψ = α is the sibling affine_primitive.

Notation. B_r(x₀) is the open ball and B̄_r(x₀) the closed ball. For an n-form g, dg = extDeriv g. For η ∈ TestFormOn univ n, exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n η ∈ TestFormOn univ (n+1) is the test form whose underlying form is extDeriv η.

1. (Cut-off.) Let ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ be Mathlib's smooth bump function (ContDiffBump) centred at x₀ with inner radius rIn := r and outer radius rOut := r + 1; this is allowed because 0 < r < r + 1. Then ζ is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff) and has compact support (ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport; ℝ^P is finite-dimensional). Moreover ζ(z) = 1 for every z ∈ B̄_r(x₀) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall), hence for every z ∈ B_r(x₀) (ball_subset_closedBall).

2. (The primitive.) Let ψ(y) := ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ · α.curryLeft(y − x₀), an n-form. ψ is C^∞: it is the continuous linear map α.curryLeft composed with the smooth map y ↦ y − x₀, multiplied by a constant (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff, ContDiff.comp, contDiff_id.sub contDiff_const, ContDiff.const_smul). By the sibling affine_primitive, extDeriv ψ y = α for every y ∈ ℝ^P.

3. (A compactly supported primitive.) Let g(y) := ζ(y) · ψ(y). g is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul applied to steps 1 and 2), and it has compact support because ζ does (HasCompactSupport.smul_right). So g is a test form with tsupport g ⊆ ℝ^P = univ, and hence η := g ∈ TestFormOn univ n.

4. (∂X = 0 kills dη.) Let dη := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n η; its underlying form is extDeriv g. By the definition of the boundary (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), X(dη) = (∂X)(η). Since ∂X = 0, X(dη) = 0(η) = 0.

5. (φ = dη on the ball.) Let y ∈ B_r(x₀). The open ball B_r(x₀) is a neighbourhood of y (isOpen_ball.mem_nhds). For z in it ζ(z) = 1 (step 1), so g(z) = ψ(z); thus g =ᶠ[𝓝 y] ψ. The exterior derivative at y depends only on the germ at y (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq), so extDeriv g y = extDeriv ψ y = α by step 2. By hypothesis φ(y) = α. Hence φ(y) = (dη)(y) for every y ∈ B_r(x₀).

6. (Localization.) B_r(x₀) is open, spt X ⊆ B_r(x₀) by hypothesis, and by step 5 the forms φ, dη ∈ TestFormOn univ (n+1) agree on B_r(x₀). The sibling localize, applied with (VO), P, k := n + 1, U := univ, G := B_r(x₀), X, φ₁ := φ and φ₂ := dη, gives X(φ) = X(dη). By step 4, X(dη) = 0. Hence X(φ) = 0. ∎

Lean note (this exact proof compiled against the pinned snapshot in a scratch file, using only the two siblings; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only):
  intro VO P n X x₀ r α φ hr hbd hspt hφ
  let ζ : ContDiffBump x₀ := ⟨r, r + 1, hr, by linarith⟩
  let ψ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n := fun y => ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft (y - x₀)
  have hψ : IsSmoothForm ψ :=
    (α.curryLeft.contDiff.comp (contDiff_id.sub contDiff_const)).const_smul _
  let g : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n := fun y => ζ y • ψ y
  have hg : IsSmoothForm g := ζ.contDiff.smul hψ
  have hgc : HasCompactSupport g := ζ.hasCompactSupport.smul_right
  let η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n := ⟨g, ⟨hg, hgc⟩, subset_univ _⟩
  have h0 : X (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n η) = 0 := by
    have h := congrArg (fun T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n => T η) hbd
    simpa using h
  have heq : EqOn (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (n + 1))
      ((exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)) :
        DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (n + 1)) (ball x₀ r) := by
    intro y hy
    rw [hφ y hy]
    change α = extDeriv g y
    have hev : g =ᶠ[𝓝 y] ψ := by
      filter_upwards [isOpen_ball.mem_nhds hy] with z hz
      simp [g, ζ.one_of_mem_closedBall (ball_subset_closedBall hz)]
    rw [hev.extDeriv_eq, Submission.cbrld_cone_extDeriv_affine_contraction P n α x₀ y]
  rw [Submission.cbrld_cone_eval_eq_of_eqOn_open VO P (n + 1) univ (ball x₀ r) X φ _ isOpen_ball hspt heq, h0]
proof_key_steps: Bump ζ (ContDiffBump at x₀, rIn = r, rOut = r + 1): smooth, compactly supported, ζ = 1 on B_r(x₀).
ψ(y) = (n+1)⁻¹ α.curryLeft(y − x₀) is smooth with dψ = α (affine_primitive); η := ζψ is a test n-form.
On the open ball ζψ = ψ, so dη = dψ = α = φ there (EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq).
localize with G = B_r(x₀) ⊇ spt X gives X(φ) = X(dη) = 0.

audit.reason: The bump with radii r and r+1 produces a compactly supported primitive. Germ locality and affine_primitive identify its exterior derivative with φ on the ball; boundary vanishing and localize then give X φ = 0. Both dependencies are correctly declared. The proof needs no finite-mass assumption and applies in the parent at radius ϱ+ε/2.
